## Overview

**scaper** (Single-Cell transcriptomics-level Cytokine Activity Prediction and Estimation) is an R package developed by **Zaoqu Liu** for quantifying cytokine signaling activity at single-cell resolution. The package integrates curated gene sets from the CytoSig and Reactome databases with the Variance-Adjusted Mahalanobis (VAM) scoring methodology.

### Key Features

- **Bidirectional Scoring**: Accounts for both up-regulated and down-regulated target genes
- **Two Database Options**: CytoSig (41 cytokines) and Reactome (30 cytokines)
- **Seurat Integration**: Seamless workflow with Seurat objects
- **High Performance**: ~0.2 ms per cell per cytokine
- **Scientific Accuracy**: Mathematically validated scoring algorithm

## Installation

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
# From R-universe (recommended)
install.packages("scaper", repos = "https://zaoqu-liu.r-universe.dev")

# From GitHub
remotes::install_github("Zaoqu-Liu/scaper")
```

## Quick Start

```{r quickstart, message=FALSE}
library(scaper)
library(Seurat)
library(SeuratObject)

# Load example data
data(pbmc_small)

# Compute cytokine activity scores for all cytokines
# Note: normalize=TRUE will handle normalization automatically
result <- scapeForSeurat(
  seurat.object = pbmc_small,
  database = "cytosig",
  cytokine = "all",
  normalize = TRUE
)

# Extract scores
scores <- GetAssayData(result, assay = "scape", layer = "data")
dim(scores)
```

## Supported Cytokines

### CytoSig Database (n = 41)

```{r cytosig}
cytosig_list <- supportedCytokines(database = "cytosig")
cat("Total:", length(cytosig_list), "cytokines\n\n")
print(cytosig_list)
```

### Reactome Database (n = 30)

```{r reactome}
reactome_list <- supportedCytokines(database = "reactome")
cat("Total:", length(reactome_list), "cytokines\n\n")
print(reactome_list)
```

## Basic Usage Examples

### Example 1: Targeted Cytokine Analysis

```{r example1}
# Focus on specific cytokines
target_cytokines <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA")

result_targeted <- scapeForSeurat(
  seurat.object = pbmc_small,
  database = "cytosig",
  cytokine = target_cytokines,
  normalize = FALSE  # Already normalized
)

# Extract and examine scores
scores_targeted <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(
  GetAssayData(result_targeted, assay = "scape", layer = "data")
)))

head(scores_targeted)
```

### Example 2: Matrix-Based Analysis

```{r example2}
# Prepare normalized expression matrix (cells × genes)
expression_data <- as.data.frame(t(as.matrix(
  GetAssayData(pbmc_small, layer = "data")
)))

# Compute cytokine activity scores
activity_scores <- scape(
  counts.matrix = expression_data,
  database = "cytosig",
  cytokine = c("IL6", "IL4", "IFNG")
)

# Result dimensions
dim(activity_scores)
head(activity_scores)
```

## Basic Visualization

```{r visualization, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
library(pheatmap)

# Prepare data for visualization (sample 20 cytokines for clarity)
set.seed(123)
sample_cytokines <- sample(colnames(scores), min(20, ncol(scores)))
plot_data <- t(scores[sample_cytokines, ])

# Create heatmap
pheatmap(
  plot_data,
  fontsize_row = 6,
  fontsize_col = 8,
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  cluster_cols = TRUE,
  main = "Cytokine Activity Heatmap (Sample)",
  color = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100)
)
```

## Activity Score Distribution

```{r distribution, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
# Examine IL6 activity distribution
il6_scores <- scores["IL6", ]

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(il6_scores, breaks = 20, col = "skyblue", 
     main = "IL6 Activity Distribution",
     xlab = "Activity Score", ylab = "Frequency")
abline(v = median(il6_scores), col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)

boxplot(il6_scores, col = "lightgreen", 
        main = "IL6 Activity Boxplot",
        ylab = "Activity Score")
```

## Summary Statistics

```{r stats}
# Calculate summary statistics for selected cytokines
selected <- c("IL6", "IFNG", "IL4", "TNFA")
stats_df <- data.frame(
  Cytokine = selected,
  Min = sapply(selected, function(x) min(scores[x, ])),
  Q1 = sapply(selected, function(x) quantile(scores[x, ], 0.25)),
  Median = sapply(selected, function(x) median(scores[x, ])),
  Mean = sapply(selected, function(x) mean(scores[x, ])),
  Q3 = sapply(selected, function(x) quantile(scores[x, ], 0.75)),
  Max = sapply(selected, function(x) max(scores[x, ])),
  SD = sapply(selected, function(x) sd(scores[x, ]))
)

knitr::kable(stats_df, digits = 3, caption = "Summary Statistics of Cytokine Activity Scores")
```

## Score Interpretation

**Activity Score Range**: [0, 1] (CDF values)

- **High (> 0.7)**: Strong evidence of cytokine pathway activation
- **Medium (0.3 - 0.7)**: Moderate or basal signaling activity
- **Low (< 0.3)**: Minimal cytokine pathway activity

## Comparison Between Methods

```{r comparison}
# Compare scape() and scapeForSeurat() results
matrix_result <- scape(expression_data, database = "cytosig", cytokine = "IL6")
seurat_result <- GetAssayData(
  scapeForSeurat(pbmc_small, database = "cytosig", cytokine = "IL6", normalize = FALSE),
  assay = "scape", layer = "data"
)

# Calculate correlation
correlation <- cor(matrix_result[, "IL6"], as.numeric(seurat_result))

cat(sprintf("Correlation between scape() and scapeForSeurat(): %.4f\n", correlation))
cat("Both methods produce highly consistent results!\n")
```
